sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Much mucus in throat at 10 p.m. (second day),®.—In the
forenoon my throat began to feel dry and hard ; at 8 p.m. it feels as if raw ;
it feels a& if something were in it; I continually try to clear it (second
day) ; throat feels much irritated (third day) ; great soreness of throat
(fourth day); throat all the way down feels as if scalded (fifth day),".—(I
have a slight sore throat and hoarseness this morning before taking the
drug; has disappeared in the evening) (first day); slight difficulty in swal¬
lowing (second day),®.—Throat feels dry and husky ; I keep swallowing con¬
tinually (second day) ; throat symptoms more severe (third day),’.—Great
dryness of the trachea, causing me to clear the throat of some foreign sub¬
stance at 11 a.m. ; throat still dry at 2 p.m. ; about an hour later (an hour
after the second dose) throat began to feel worse, causing me to cough and
try to clear it as much as possible; this irritation continued all day; I feel,
while in a close room, as if I could not get air enough ; feel much better
while out of doors (fourth day); but little irritation of the throat in a cool
room or in the fresh air; but the same as before in a close room, though
not so much as last night, in the morning ; throat felt dry in the afternoon,
then after two hours it became quite moist, and there was great expectoration
(fifth day); all the throat symptoms have gone at 4 p.m.; irritation of the
trachea m a close room at 8 p.m., disappearing on going into the fresh air
(seventh day),’.—Have had continued irritation of the pharynx and trachea,
cairsing a continued short, hacking cough, with an accumulation of mucus,
which I must expectorate (third day),’.—A sharp pain through the uvula,
causing the tears to start (fifteen minutes after second dose),’,

Stoaiach. — Not much appetite (fourth day),® — [30.] Great thirst

pressed (second day),'.—On reclining or lying down my chest feels dis¬
tressed, as from deficient aeration of blood in the lungs (third day),'.

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
In a few moments after retiring (after the second dose) I be¬
gan to feel cold ; pulse at the wrist very weak, intermitting one or two
beats; once it stopped for a few seconds; this was followed by a bounding
pulse; I became very warm, and my breathing stopped ; my lungs felt as
if I were breathing in hot air (fifth day),'.—Feet and hands cold; head
hot (seventh day),'.

TRIMETHYLAMINUM.

Trimethylamin, CgHyN.

Preparation, solutions.

An alkaloid found in the following plants; Chenopodium vulvaria, Cra-
ttegus oxycantha, Sorbus aucuparia. Phallus impudicus, Pyrus communis.
Arnica montana. Cotyledon umbilicus, Fagus sylvatica, etc.; also in
Herring-brine, Cod liver oil, etc.

Authority. M. Dujardin-Beaumetz, Nouvelles Recherches sur la Trime-
thylamine, Paris, 1873; 1. effects on himself, of 50 centigrams of the mu¬
riate dissolved in water; 2 , another person in perfect health took 75 centi¬
grams of the muriate; 3, results of several experiments.

This drug, according to several experiments on patients, etc., diminishes
the amount of urea; in one case there was a diminution of over 2 grams
during twenty-four hours, in another 2.24 grams, in another a diminution
of 3 grams,®.—Pulse 88 (before the experiment) ; 84 (after one hour) ; 82
(later) ; 76 (after two hours). There was not only a diminution in the
number of pulsations, but also a modification in the force, as shown by
the tracing (it shows no special modification, with the exception of dimi¬
nution in the force of the heart’s action),®.—Pulse 78 (before the exper¬
iment) ; 76 (after one hour); 74 (after one hour and a half); 72 (after
two hours); 78 (after four hours),'.—Temperature 37.4° (before the experi¬
ment) ; 37.2° (after one hour); 37° (after one hour and a half); 36.8° (after
two hours),'.—Temperature 37° (before the experiment); 36.8° (after one
hour) ; 36.4° (later); 36° (after two hours),®.

chest, from 9 to 11 a.m. (tenth day),l

Heart a/tid Pulse. —Dull pain in the region of the heart, rendered
sharp by drawing a long breath, at 4 p.m. (second day),^—Darting rheu¬
matic pains in region of heart (tenth day),l— [ 80 .] Pulse full and quick,
100, at 9 A.M. (usually 70); at 11 a.m. it had returned to its normal con¬
dition (tenth day),^—Pulse intermittent,^

Hack. —Aching pain in the small of the back, with the fever (seventh
day),^

sections.label: Extremities
sections.text:
Heaviness of all the limbs,®.—Shooting pains in left
heel and left wrist (fifth day),'*.—Shooting pains in different joints, during
the day (sixteenth day),*.—In the afternoon and evening, shooting pains
in the joints of the upper and lower extremities (seventeenth day),*.—
Shooting pains (slight) in the different joints (eighteenth and nineteenth
days),*.

Superior Extremities.—Shoulder. Rheumatic aching pain in
left shoulder (ninth day),®.—Pain in the left shoulder (tenth day),®.— [ 90 .]
Severe shocks in left shoulder-joint, every few minutes, lasting the en¬
tire afternoon (sixth day); lasting all the forenoon (seventh day),'*.
— Severe shooting pains in right shoulder-joint, at 2 P.M. (fifth day),*.—
Shooting pains in the right shoulder, in the forenoon (fifteenth day),*.—
Shooting pains in elbows, wrists, and finger-joints at different times, all the
forenoon (ninth day )f—ElhoiV . In the forenoon, frequent shooting pains
in the elbow, wrist, and finger-joints of the right side (eleventh day),*.—
Forearm. Dull pain in the bones of the left forearm, at 12 m. (ninth
day),*.—Dull intermittent pain in left forearm, at 11 p.m., afterwards same
shooting pains that seem to be characteristic of this remedy (third day),*.
—Aching down the left forearm (tenth day),®.—Frequently occurring pain
in the left forearm of a dull nature, in the forenoon (eleventh day),*.—
Wrist. At 4 P.M. a sharp stinging pain at a single small spot on the inner

side of the dorsum of the wrist, lasting about a minute (fourteenth day),*._

[ 100 .] Pains in right wrist-joint, at first shooting and intermittent, after¬
wards constant, lasting a few minutes, at 12 m. (fourteenth day),*,—Shoot-

Fingevs. Shooting pain in phalangeal joints of third finger, and' at

—A stinging pain in the palmar surface of right thumb, ungual phalanx

Inferior Extremities.—Hip. Dull pain in left hip-joint, felt
only after rising from a sitting posture and attempting to walk, and which
produced a limping gait; this pain was felt every time an attempt to walk
was made, during several hours; it usually wore off each time after tak¬
ing a few steps (fourteenth day),''.— ThigJt, Tearing pain in lower part
of left thigh, at 2.30 p.m. (second day),'.—Flying sharp pain in the right

(eighth day),®.—Rheumatic aching pain in left knee (ninth day),®.— [ 110 .]
Slight intermitting pains in the right knee-joint, at 9 a.m. (fourteenth
day),'.—ief/. Boring pain in right tibia, during the forenoon (twelfth
Fnlile. Dull pain in the left ankle, inner part made sharp, by
bearing weight on it, at 12 p.m. (sixth day),'.—Shooting pains in right

Genera I Hies .— Inability to keep quiet,®. — Weakness (eleventh day),®.
—AVeakness, especially in the knees, after a stool (thirteenth day),'.—
[ 120 .] Great weakness, able to walk about some, but easily tired (eighth

the heart (eleventh day),®.—Felt better in the open air,®.

sections.label: Skin
sections.text:
Itching in spots on the chin and among the whiskers,®.—Pim¬
ples on the back of the neck, in the evening (fourteenth day),'.—Itching
sensation about the neck and on the chin, among the whiskers, in the even¬
ing (fourteenth day),'.

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Almost constant inclination to gape (third day),'.—Constant
disposition to gape, through the day (third day),'.—Constant inclination
to gape, in the afternoon (tenth day),'.—Sleepiness (after five hours),'.—
[ 130 .] Restless during sleep,'.—Wakeful and restless, after 4 a.m. (eighth
day),'.—Lewd dreams during the night (seventh day),'.

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Chilliness felt during the night, more in the morning, on wak¬
ing,'.—Chilliness along the spine, with the stool (seventh morning),®.—In
the afternoon had fever, with pulsation of the arteries of the head, and
dull aching in the occiput, and with this an aching pain in the small of
the back (seventh day),®.

32 TUSSILAGO FRAGRANS—TUSSILAGO PETASITES.

TUSSILAGO FRAGRANS.

Petasites fragrans, Moen.

Natural order, Corapositae.

Common name, Italian or fragrant Tussilage.

Preparation, Tincture of whole plant.

Authority. Dr. Demeures, Jonrn. de la Soc. Gall., vol. iv, p. 109, three
drops on the tongue.

Ml nd. —State of mind such that I was satisfied with everything;
everything about me seemed pleasing; serenity of disposition ; benevolence
of language; I could engage in discussions of the most exciting interest
with calmness, while making use of the most appropriate expressions; in
fine, entering upon them without hesitation, and succeeding in them, being
beforehand confident of success (fifth to tenth day).—Complaining mood,
finding fault with everything, making spiteful remarks, the nature of which
he does not himself recognize, and is astonished that others are offended at
them ; for this reason, when aware of their character, he remains silent for
fear of offending his associates (after four hours).

Hend. —Transient headache, like a stupefaction ; feeling of intoxica¬
tion, as after the abuse of spirituous liquors (after two hours).

JEye. —Dryness of the eyes, when looking about in the open air, forcing
them to wink often (after two hours).

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Acidity in the oesophagus, like heartburn, ceasing entirely
after dinner (after two hours).

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
It seems as if there were at the bottom of the cardia a
morsel which will not pass down (after half an hour).

Inferior Ext remit les. — Weakness in the legs (after two hours).
—Pain from side to side in the tarsus, between that and the metatarsus of
the left foot, when walking; this pain does not last long, but returns often
(second to fifth day).—Pain in the metatarsal joint, as if caused by a blow
(after two hours).

Generalities. —[10.] January 5th (ninth day) I started for Toulon ;
I returned thence on the 12th, stouter in person than on my departure. I
often take this journey, and at my return I always have been reduced in
flesh, owing to irregular diet. From January 10th to February 5th, this
increase in size continued, and was perceptible to myself; but, on the other
hand, I felt, after the lOth of January, a degree of plethora, which might
easily have overcome me. The abdomen, which had a tendency to cor¬
pulency, was reduced to its normal size. Eight years later it had not yet
regained that former protuberance.

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
I sleep less, and find myself none the worse for it, a circum¬
stance which certainly never occurred to me before (after two weeks).

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Sweat and heat of the skin, caused by slight exertion, such as
never had caused perspiration (after half an hour).
